evidence: The report establishes that RTX video enhancement activates in Edge but not Peek, and identifies missing browser-profile preference keys.
BrowserControl creates its own WebView2 environment using Peek temporary user data rather than the interactive Edge profile.
The inspected initialization does not expose a supported PowerToys setting that promises NVIDIA RTX video enhancement or imports the Edge browser preference.
judgment.recommended_action: Clarify separate WebView2 settings and frame enhancement support as a feature request with runtime/GPU capability evidence.
judgment.rationale: A separate embedded browser profile explains why Edge preferences are not inherited; it does not prove which GPU/runtime versions support enhancement inside WebView2. Adding such integration is a feature/compatibility investigation, not justification for editing transient profile JSON or claiming a missing supported toggle.

fix_assessment.rationale: No existing Peek contract to inherit Edge RTX-enhancement preferences is established; this is a requested integration capability rather than a demonstrated regression in that contract.

title: Peek does not enable NVIDIA RTX Super Resolution for videos

comment.body: Peek uses an embedded WebView2 environment with its own profile, not your interactive Edge profile. Enabling video enhancement in Edge therefore does not automatically configure Peek. The missing preference keys alone do not establish that adding them would enable supported RTX enhancement in WebView2, and editing Peek temporary profile files is not a durable setting. This is better tracked as a request to investigate supported video-enhancement integration for Peek, with the relevant WebView2 and driver capabilities, rather than as an instruction to copy Edge preferences.

inferences: The exact video enhancement support of the reporter WebView2/GPU stack is not established by absence of two JSON preference fields.
